title: Slot marketplace concept notes
body:
Overview:

This doc captures early UX/wireframe thinking for a 'Slot Marketplace' experience inside the Dedicated Capacity console. The core idea: provide customers a market-style interface to discover, book, trade, and manage reserved GPU time slices (slots) across dedicated pools to increase utilization flexibility and lower unit cost for bursty workloads.

Why we need it (problem statement):
- Customers buy Dedicated GPU pools to get predictable throughput but often underutilize committed capacity due to seasonality/spiky jobs.
- Current reservation UI is siloed: create reservation -> consumes capacity. There is no first-class path to reassign or temporarily trade excess capacity between teams or for short-term bursts.
- Platform-side autoscaling and bursts are helpful, but customers want visibility and control (price, priority, duration) when choosing to buy extra capacity or release unused reservations.

Goals (product + UX):
1) Give customers an easy way to list available slots (their org's and marketplace), filter by region/GPU/latency tier, and compare price vs. fallback SLOs.
2) Provide safe trade/resale primitives: a team can list unused reservation time, set minimum price and constraints (region, model compatibility), and transfer or rent to a teammate or org unit.
3) Simplify burst buying: short-term spot-style slots for immediate capacity with clear latency/availability expectations and automatic fallback policies.
4) Keep operations simple: preserve existing SLAs and autoscale rules while adding marketplace flows that respect entitlements and billing.

Primary personas:
- Platform Engineer (Alice): wants to reallocate unused reservations across teams without opening tickets.
- ML Prod Owner (Ben): needs cheap short bursts for eval and is willing to accept lower priority to save cost.
- Capacity Planner (Carmen): wants visibility into utilization and marketplace activity to inform commits.

High-level flows (wireframe focus):
A) Marketplace discovery -> booking (fast path)
  - Top bar: scope selector (Org / Team / Pool), search, filters (GPU type, region, min-duration, max-price, availability window).
  - Grid/list view: each card shows slot-id, provider (self/other-team/Redwood-spot), GPU type, start-end window, price per GPU-hour, priority tier (guaranteed vs spot), compatibility tags (kv-cache friendly, quantized-only), and quick actions (Book / Preview SLA).
  - Quick-book modal: show expected latency histogram, fallback models/pools, cost estimate, confirmation CTA. Include 'auto-fallback' checkbox with policy selector (nearest region, cheaper model variant, or queue).

B) Reservation listing + resale (seller flow)
  - Reservation detail panel: reservation metadata, usage timeline, remaining hours, linked runtime config, scope controls (can be listed if team-owned and > X hours remaining).
  - List-for-sale modal: set listing duration, minimum price, allowed buyers (org-wide / specific teams), visibility (private/public), and penalty terms (early-cancel fee). Provide an approve flow that generates an escrow-like hold.
  - Activity feed: show offers, accepted trades, and automatic changes to reservation ownership.

C) Burst/spot buying (buyer flow)
  - Spot marketplace tab with slider for max price vs latency. Price-time curve visualization: lower price -> lower probability of successful immediate allocation.
  - On accept: present fallback chain and an offer expiration timer. Clear language about preemption risk and SLO degradation implications.

Key UI components (wireframe primitives):
- Slot Card: small square with GPU icon, price tag, duration bar (mini timeline), badges (spot/guaranteed/team-shared), and hover detail.
- Timeline scrubber: compact view showing pool commitments over next 30 days with color bands for reserved vs available vs listed-for-sale.
- Quick-compare drawer: select up to 3 slots and compare costs, latencies, and compatibility.
- Negotiation widget (optional v2): buyer can propose a counter-price; seller can accept or auto-accept above threshold.

Acceptance criteria / Metrics to track:
- Flow success rate: % of discovery-to-book completions without manual support. Target 85% in pilot.
- Utilization lift: increase org-wide reserved pool utilization by 10–20% over baseline in 90 days.
- Time-to-burst: median time from spot request to allocation < 60s for immediate-available slots.
- Revenue/credits moved through marketplace (for internal chargeback) tracked by transaction events.

Safety, billing, and policy constraints:
- Listings must respect contractual commitments: cannot list slots that would violate minimum committed utilization terms without penalty.
- Ownership transitions must trigger audit events and billing transfers. Keep escrow to avoid double-spend.
- Prevent cross-region mismatches unless explicitly allowed (region-locked slots).
- Integrate with KMS/audit logs for Private deployments; trades must be visible in customer audit trail.

Edge cases / unresolved questions:
- Pricing model: fixed-per-hour vs dynamic auction. For v1 prefer fixed listings + Redwood-managed spot bucket for instant bursts.
- How to handle preempted workloads: provide automated checkpointing hooks (customers opt-in) and recommended snapshotters in docs.
- If a listed reservation is partially used during a pending offer, how to reconcile? Proposal: mark listing as 'tentative' and require minimum remaining hours when listing.
- Billing reconciliation for prorated reservations spanning billing cycles.

Wireframe notes (low-fi):
- Workspace -> Dedicated -> Marketplace (tabbed) -> Overview grid + timeline + my-reservations list.
- Use vertical split: left = filters + pools; center = slot grid + compare drawer; right = detail panel + activity feed.
- Colour system: green = guaranteed, amber = soft-guarantee, red outline = spot/preemptible.

Prototype acceptance checklist (dev handoff):
- Clickable prototype (Figma) with: filter interactions, quick-book modal with cost calc, seller list flow, timeline scrubber update on booking.
- Backend contracts: REST endpoints to list slots, create listing, accept offer, transfer reservation, query compatibility. Draft API stubs: /api/v1/capacity/slots, /api/v1/capacity/listings, /api/v1/capacity/transactions.
- Telemetry keys: marketplace.listing_created, marketplace.offer_accepted, marketplace.booking_failed, marketplace.transfer_completed.

Next steps / backlog items (recommended prioritization):
1) Design spike: build Figma skeleton of Marketplace flows and get 3 PM/Platform/CS reviews (2w) — owner: Lina.
2) Backend proof-of-concept: internal-only listing and transfer simulation (4w, eng infra + billing) — owner: Evan.
3) Pilot with 2 internal teams for cross-team trading (6w) — owner: Priya.
4) UX polish + docs + checkout SLAs (2w) — owner: Design.

Open requests / asks for reviewers:
- Platform leads: validate policy constraints (min-commit rules, penalties).
- Billing: confirm feasible escrow/transfer mechanics and event hooks for audit.
- SRE: give rough bounds on allocation latency for spot-style immediate requests and recommended limits for safety.

Sign-off checklist (pre-PRD):
- Confirmation on pricing model (fixed vs auction)
- Agreement on minimum listing length and penalty schedule
- API surface accepted by infra and billing

Notes to self / rough ideas to explore later:
- 'Credit swap' primitive for internal orgs where teams can exchange credits instead of money to reassign reservations.
- Auto-list-if-unused: option to auto-list unused reservations after X% idle for Y days.
- Marketplace insights page: heatmap of demand by region/time to inform future commit guidance.

----
This is intentionally a conceptual doc (draft). Aim is to capture multiple approaches; next step is to convert the favored approach into a short PRD and Figma wireframes.
